prompt: docker cheatsheet, include compose v2 stuff and the newer buildkit features. i always mix up the old and new syntax

usability.notes: Excellent organization across two well-named pages (Core & Build / Compose V2 & Production) with a logical flow from fundamentals to advanced. Section 11 (Old vs New Syntax Guide) directly addresses the user's stated pain point ('I always mix up the old and new syntax') with a two-column legacy/modern comparison — a standout design choice. Visual variety is strong throughout: RefRows for command references, Code blocks for copy-pasteable examples, Bullets for conceptual notes, KV pairs for flag glossaries, and the card grid in Section 24 for decision guidance. Information density is well-calibrated — nearly every section has 5–7 items plus a code block, hitting the substantive-but-digestible sweet spot. The highlight-background tip callouts add helpful scannable asides without bloating sections. The Section 24 'When to Use What' grid is a professional-grade desk reference addition. Minor deduction not warranted — this is bookmark-worthy.

completeness.notes: Comprehensively covers everything the prompt asked for and then some. Core CLI (Sections 1–3) and Dockerfile essentials (4) provide solid grounding. BuildKit is covered at two depths: fundamentals (5) and advanced cache/secret/SSH mounts (6) — exactly the kind of detail practitioners need. Multi-stage builds (7) is thorough with cross-stage COPY patterns. Compose V2 gets five dedicated sections: CLI differences (12), file structure with healthcheck conditions (13), service config (14), networking with internal: true (15), volumes with long syntax (16), build config with cache_from/cache_to (17), profiles & overrides (18), and the new `develop.watch` feature (19). The old-vs-new syntax comparison directly answers the user's stated confusion. Bonus coverage of multi-platform buildx (20), logging/debugging (21), security best practices (22), resource constraints (23), and the decision guide (24) are all genuinely useful extras. No meaningful gaps: healthchecks, restart policies, secrets, env/ARG, tmpfs, network aliases, and registry operations are all present.

accuracy.notes: All 8 verified claims matched official Docker documentation exactly. The cheatsheet is technically precise across BuildKit, Compose V2, lifecycle signals, Compose Watch, multi-platform builds, and file naming conventions. No invented flags, no outdated syntax presented as current, no incorrect API signatures. The one minor imprecision — describing `docker kill` as "immediate SIGKILL" without noting it accepts `--signal` — is harmless since the default is indeed SIGKILL and the description won't break any user workflow. The Compose Watch `develop.watch` actions (`sync`, `rebuild`, `sync+restart`) are all confirmed correct per the Compose Develop Specification. The `--platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64` multi-platform buildx syntax is correct. Overall, this is an exceptionally accurate cheatsheet with no meaningful errors found across all 8 targeted verifications.

verified_claims.claim: BuildKit is enabled by default in Docker Desktop and Docker 23.0+
verified_claims.evidence: Docker Engine 23.0 release notes confirm: 'Docker v23.0 now uses BuildKit by default to build Linux images.' Confirmed at docs.docker.com/build/buildkit/ and docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/23.0/

verified_claims.claim: docker compose (V2) is a CLI plugin — no separate binary needed
verified_claims.evidence: Docker docs confirm Compose V2 'functions as a Docker CLI plugin' installed to $DOCKER_CONFIG/cli-plugins/, included by default in Docker Desktop. docs.docker.com/compose/install/

verified_claims.claim: compose.yaml is the recommended filename, replacing docker-compose.yml
verified_claims.evidence: Docker Compose spec confirms: 'The default path for a Compose file is compose.yaml (preferred)... Compose also supports docker-compose.yaml and docker-compose.yml for backwards compatibility.' docs.docker.com/compose/intro/compose-application-model/

verified_claims.claim: docker stop sends SIGTERM first, then SIGKILL after grace period
verified_claims.evidence: Docker docs: 'The main process inside the container will receive SIGTERM, and after a grace period, SIGKILL.' Default timeout is 10s on Linux. docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/stop/

verified_claims.claim: depends_on supports condition: service_healthy in Compose V2
verified_claims.evidence: Docker Compose docs confirm service_healthy condition: 'Compose guarantees dependency services marked with service_healthy are healthy before starting a dependent service.' docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/startup-order/

verified_claims.claim: compose.override.yaml is automatically merged on top of compose.yaml
verified_claims.evidence: Docker docs: 'By default, Compose reads two files, a compose.yaml and an optional compose.override.yaml file. When you run docker compose up it reads the overrides automatically.' docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/multiple-compose-files/merge/

verified_claims.claim: Compose Watch supports three actions: sync, rebuild, and sync+restart
verified_claims.evidence: Compose Develop Specification confirms all three actions with exact descriptions matching the cheatsheet. docs.docker.com/reference/compose-file/develop/ and docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/file-watch/

verified_claims.claim: docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 --push for multi-arch images
verified_claims.evidence: Docker multi-platform docs confirm: 'docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 .' is the correct syntax. Comma-separated list matches what the cheatsheet's line-continuation renders. docs.docker.com/build/building/multi-platform/
